title: Internet Watch Foundation reports huge rise in AI child sexual abuse material
key_facts: The UK-based Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) assessed 6,310 AI images meeting the legal definition of child sexual abuse material in the first half of 2026.
That is 40% above last year's total of more than 4,500.
Figures cover still images only; videos have also surged.
Most images showed girls aged seven to 13.
IWF calls for new statutory regulation of AI; the UK government has not signalled an imminent AI bill.
It is illegal in the UK to adapt or distribute AI models to create such material; developing one carries up to five years in prison.
Report Remove received 420 reports from children about faked explicit images so far this year, above 397 for all of 2025.
quote_evidence: It is incumbent on tech companies to build tools which cannot be abused this way.
UK law is clear that child sexual abuse material is illegal, regardless of whether it is AI-generated or not.
why_it_matters_hint: Half-year total already exceeds all of 2025.
event_date: First half of 2026 data, reported 5 Oct 2026
